title: bpm.api_tenant_context uses threadlocal storage; worker threads spawned mid-test don't inherit the spawning thread's tenant context, causing pool.acquire() to fall back to search_path=public
summary: Discovered while implementing and verifying the ISS-0095 fix (GitHub #349). tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig's TC-EE-10-05 spawns two std.Thread.spawn worker threads, each of which calls pool.acquire() independently. src/api/tenant_context.zig stores the current tenant id in a `threadlocal var`, so a .set() call made on the spawning/main thread (whether inside makePool() per the ISS-0095 fix, or inside TestHarness.init()) is invisible to the worker threads' own thread-local storage. Each worker thread's pool.acquire() therefore sees no tenant context set on ITS thread and falls back to search_path=public, where the business tables the worker needs no longer exist post-GBL-073. This is architecturally distinct from ISS-0095 (which was about a missing .set() call on the calling thread entirely) -- it cannot be fixed by editing makePool(), since makePool() already runs (and now correctly sets context) on the main thread before any worker thread is spawned.

root_cause.details: src/api/tenant_context.zig's tenant-id storage is declared as a Zig `threadlocal var`. Any std.Thread.spawn()'d worker thread starts with its own zero-initialized copy of that threadlocal storage, regardless of what the parent thread had set. TC-EE-10-05 in tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig relies on both worker threads sharing the same tenant-scoped pool connections as the main test thread, but each worker's first pool.acquire() call resolves tenant context independently and gets the threadlocal's zero-value (empty/unset), triggering pool.zig's documented empty-context-means-public fallback.

files_to_change: Needs a design decision before implementation: options include (a) passing an explicit tenant-id parameter into worker thread entry functions and having them call api_tenant_context.set() as their first statement, (b) a pool-level API that accepts an explicit tenant id per-acquire rather than relying on ambient threadlocal state, or (c) restructuring tenant_context storage to not be threadlocal (would need concurrency-safety review, since the whole point of threadlocal here appears to be avoiding cross-request tenant leakage in a multi-threaded server). Affected test: tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig (TC-EE-10-05). Possible production-code implication: any production code path that spawns worker threads and expects them to inherit request-scoped tenant context would have the same gap -- worth a broader grep for std.Thread.spawn usage in src/ as part of the eventual fix's investigation, not assumed here.
resolution: Fixed in tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig (TC-EE-10-05 worker.run): the spawned worker thread now calls bpm.api_tenant_context.set("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000") as its first statement, before calling setInstanceError (which internally calls pool.acquire()). This mirrors the identical, already-proven pattern used in tests/integration/concurrent_instances_test.zig (completionThread) and tests/integration/iss102_claim_test.zig (claimWorkerThread) for the same class of bug. No production code changed: a grep of std.Thread.spawn across src/ (4 call sites: webhook/dispatcher.zig CaptureServer.run [test-only HTTP capture loop], identity/provider/bootstrap.zig KcHttpCallState.threadFn [pure Keycloak HTTP client call, no DB], api/routes/onboarding.zig runSagaBackground [DOES call pool.acquire() via executeSaga, but every table it touches either has public as its sole canonical home or explicitly overrides search_path itself rather than relying on ambient threadlocal routing], and lua/timeout.zig watchdogLoop [atomics only, no DB]) found no production-severity gap. Verified with a stash-based control: reverting just the fix line reproduces TC-EE-10-05 failing at std.testing.expect(r1_ok or r2_ok) (both threads see error.PersistenceFailed from search_path=public routing); restoring the fix and re-running zig build test-integration (properly-sequenced, with clean_test_db) shows zero failures referencing instance_error_test.zig across 3 separate runs. Full investigation and fix-direction rationale in src/design/fix-ISS-0097.md.

occurrences.context: Found by BACKEND-DEV while implementing the ISS-0095 fix. Confirmed pre-existing via git stash: the pre-fix baseline fails this same test even earlier (at def_store.create(), before the worker threads are even spawned), so this is not a regression introduced by the ISS-0095 fix -- the fix gets the test further along (past the main-thread setup) but does not reach a passing state due to this separate gap.

prevention: When adding new tests that spawn worker threads and touch tenant-scoped resources, explicitly call bpm.api_tenant_context.set(...) as the first statement inside the spawned thread's own entry function — never assume it inherits the spawning thread's threadlocal state. This is now the third test file in this repo to need this exact fix (concurrent_instances_test.zig, iss102_claim_test.zig, instance_error_test.zig); a shared test-helper wrapper for "spawn a worker that needs tenant context" would prevent a fourth recurrence, but was judged out of scope for this MINOR/test-only fix (adds new shared test infrastructure for a pattern that, while recurring, is a 2-line fix each time it is hit).

Production-impact check for std.Thread.spawn + pool.acquire() interaction performed and documented in src/design/fix-ISS-0097.md §1.4-1.5 — re-run this grep if new background-thread work is added to any request-handling path, since the current "safe by construction" conclusion for onboarding.zig depends on every table its background thread touches having public as its sole/canonical home or explicitly overriding search_path; a future addition to that saga that assumes ambient tenant-scoped routing would reintroduce this exact class of bug in production, as already happened once at ISS-0070/GH-285 (filed separately, see related_issues).

related_issues.relation: ISS-0070/GH-285 is the production occurrence of this exact architectural gap (background saga thread never inheriting threadlocal tenant context), discovered as a currently-live regression during this issue's mandatory production-impact investigation. Filed/updated and forwarded to the global queue separately — NOT fixed by this issue's test-only change.
